current_activity: Stoottroepen, a few hundred strong, concentrated in the polder, fail to prevent the blowing of the IJsselmeerdijk at noon
notes: Event date: 17 April 1945 (de Jong, Het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden in de Tweede Wereldoorlog, deel 10b, pp. 1314-1315). Event definition: At 12:00 that day the Wehrmacht blew the IJsselmeerdijk of the Wieringermeerpolder at two points, and the polder (about 20,000 ha) began to flood; the warning had been given to the Dutch authorities at 04:00. Stoottroepen of the Noordhollandse BS, a few hundred strong, had been concentrated in the polder to put the German demolition party out of action, but they were unable to prevent the destruction. Some of those stoottroepen, mainly former KP members, had wanted to act before the 17th; others waited for an order from Lt. Col. J. G. M. Wastenecker, commandant of the BS in Noord-Holland Noord, which did not come (he judged the Wehrmacht in the Kop van Noord-Holland too strong to act successfully without Allied support, which had not been promised). Event support: one source family (de Jong's official history, volume 10b, read directly in NIOD's page-tagged CC-BY edition; printed pages cited, paraphrase only). These stoottroepen belong to this North-Holland BS command, not to the southern NL-INF-STOOT. Location: Wieringermeer Polder, Noord-Holland, an area with a precision of 10 km. current_activity: From Medemblik, members of the stoottroepen bring some of the abandoned weapons in the polder to safety
notes: Event date: shortly after the inundation of 17 April 1945, represented as 18 April (de Jong, Het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden in de Tweede Wereldoorlog, deel 10b, p. 1316). Event definition: From Medemblik, where a Centrale Commissie Wieringermeer was set up, attempts began soon afterwards to recover property left in the polder; members of the stoottroepen succeeded in bringing some of the abandoned weapons to safety.
